standard.title: Develop questions about past and present
standard.description: develop questions about objects, people, places and events in the past and present
standard.prior_knowledge: From Foundation (AC9HSFS01): Students posed questions about familiar objects, people, places and events using basic stems (What, Where, Who, Why, How).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop questions about objects, people, places and events in the past and present to guide inquiry.

nodes.label: Questions about the past and present
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can generate questions about objects, people, places and events in both the past and present, using 'where', 'what', 'how' and 'why' stems.
nodes.minimum_width: Generate at least two questions about a provided source — one about the present and one about the past — using at least two different question stems.
nodes.typical_width: Pose questions using Where, What, How and Why stems about families and places when provided with everyday objects, photos, maps and observation sketches; ask questions before, during and after listening to stories about people and places.
wider: Prepare a set of questions for parents or grandparents about how and where they lived in the past and the places they value
Sort questions about the past and present and discuss what type of source would best answer each question
nodes.hinge_reason: Year 1 inquiry requires students to direct questions to the past as well as the present — students who only ask about now cannot drive the historical comparison tasks that HASS Year 1 requires.

response_modes.reason: Past-directed questions require students to imagine a time they cannot directly observe — model the cognitive move explicitly: 'To find out about the past, we ask questions like...'

success_criteria: Generates at least one question about the past and one about the present
Uses at least two different question stems (Where, What, How, Why)

nodes.label: Questions that guide inquiry
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop inquiry questions that would guide an investigation about families and places, and identify appropriate sources that would help answer them.
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least two inquiry questions about families or places and identify one source that could help answer each question.
nodes.typical_width: Prepare questions for parents and grandparents about how and where they lived; develop questions before, during and after listening to stories about people and places; identify which sources (objects, photos, maps, oral histories) best answer which questions.
wider: Develop questions specifically designed to reveal perspectives of people from different generations or backgrounds
Evaluate whether provided questions are answerable from available sources, and revise unanswerable questions

response_modes.reason: Question development for inquiry integrates source awareness with historical curiosity — the inquiry interview is the integration task.

success_criteria: Develops at least two questions that would genuinely guide an inquiry
Identifies a source that could help answer each question
